In the dry season, fire brigades start the day with one question: **where has fire appeared in the
protected areas since yesterday?** INPE publishes the fire hotspots detected by several satellites many
times an hour, in open files.

The script I used read the hotspots from the ArcGIS Online *Living Atlas* and only worked with an
institutional account. Here the hotspots come straight from **INPE's server**, with no login.

![Fire hotspots of the last 48 hours in the example area (queried on 2026-10-29).](../imagens/artigos/focos_48h.png){fig-alt="Map of the Novo Progresso region with protected areas in light green, the surrounding band in yellow and fire hotspots as points: red in the last 24 hours and orange between 24 and 48 hours. The largest concentration is in the Tapajós Environmental Protection Area."}

## Where the hotspots come from

| Source | Address | Update |
|---|---|---|
| **INPE, daily file** | `https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/diario/Brasil/focos_diario_br_YYYYMMDD.csv` | today's file grows during the day |
| INPE, every 10 minutes | `https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/10min/` | 10 minutes |
| NASA FIRMS (VIIRS and MODIS) | `https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/data/active_fire/suomi-npp-viirs-c2/csv/SUOMI_VIIRS_C2_South_America_48h.csv` | a few hours; `_24h` and `_7d` files also exist |

The INPE file has one row per hotspot, with `lat`, `lon`, `data_hora_gmt` (date and time in UTC),
`satelite`, `municipio`, `estado`, `bioma` and other fields.

::: {.callout-important}
## A hotspot is not burned area
A hotspot is a **hot pixel** seen by a satellite at one moment. The same fire shows up as dozens of
hotspots, and the same hotspot can be seen by several satellites. Use hotspots to **raise alerts** and to
compare periods with the **reference satellite** (`AQUA_M-T`). For burned area, use DETER burn scars or
MapBiomas Fire.
:::

## What you will do

1. Download the files for **today, yesterday and the day before** (to cover a full 48 hours).
2. Turn `lon` and `lat` into **points** (SIRGAS 2000).
3. Filter by **time** (in UTC, as in the file).
4. Find out **which protected area** (or surroundings) each hotspot fell in.
5. Count by protected area, time window and satellite.

## The code

Names in Portuguese: `focos` = hotspots, `pasta` = folder, `agora` = now, `dia` = day, `corte` = cutoff,
`janela` = time window, `ultimos` = latest.

::: {.panel-tabset group="programa"}

## ArcGIS Pro

```python
import arcpy
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

arcpy.env.overwriteOutput = True
gpkg = r"C:\dados\artigos.gpkg"
pasta = r"C:\dados\focos"
url = ("https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/diario/"
       "Brasil/focos_diario_br_{}.csv")

# 1 and 2. Download the three days and create the points
agora = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
pontos = []
for i in range(3):
    dia = (agora - timedelta(days=i)).strftime("%Y%m%d")
    csv = rf"{pasta}\focos_{dia}.csv"
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(url.format(dia), csv)
    pontos.append(arcpy.management.XYTableToPoint(
        csv, rf"memory\focos_{dia}", "lon", "lat",
        coordinate_system=arcpy.SpatialReference(4674)))
focos = arcpy.management.Merge(pontos, r"memory\focos")

# 3 and 4. Protected area of each hotspot and filter for the last 48 hours
focos_ucs = arcpy.analysis.PairwiseIntersect([focos, gpkg + r"\main.ucs"], r"memory\focos_ucs")
corte_48h = (agora - timedelta(hours=48)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
ultimos = arcpy.analysis.Select(focos_ucs, r"C:\dados\resultados.gdb\focos_ucs_48h",
                                f"data_hora_gmt >= timestamp '{corte_48h}'")

# 5. Count by protected area and satellite
arcpy.analysis.Statistics(ultimos, r"C:\dados\resultados.gdb\focos_por_uc",
                          [["id", "COUNT"]], ["nome_uc", "satelite"])
```

::: {.callout-note}
`XYTableToPoint` reads `data_hora_gmt` as text or as a date, depending on the ArcGIS Pro version. If
`Select` finds nothing, check the field type and change the filter to
`data_hora_gmt >= '{corte_48h}'`, which compares the text.
:::

## QGIS

```python
import os, tempfile, urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import processing

G = "C:/dados/artigos.gpkg"
url = ("https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/diario/"
       "Brasil/focos_diario_br_{}.csv")

def rodar(alg, **p):
    p.setdefault("OUTPUT", "memory:")
    return processing.run(alg, p)["OUTPUT"]

# 1 and 2. Download the three days and open them as point layers (delimited text)
agora = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
camadas = []
for i in range(3):
    dia = (agora - timedelta(days=i)).strftime("%Y%m%d")
    csv = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), f"focos_{dia}.csv")
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(url.format(dia), csv)
    uri = (f"file:///{csv}?delimiter=,&xField=lon&yField=lat&crs=EPSG:4674"
           "&field=data_hora_gmt:text")
    camadas.append(QgsVectorLayer(uri, f"focos_{dia}", "delimitedtext"))
focos = rodar("native:mergevectorlayers", LAYERS=camadas, CRS="EPSG:4674")

# 3. Last 48 hours (text in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format compares like a date)
corte = (agora - timedelta(hours=48)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
focos = rodar("native:extractbyexpression", INPUT=focos,
              EXPRESSION=f"\"data_hora_gmt\" >= '{corte}'")

# 4. Protected area of each hotspot (predicate 5 = "within")
focos_ucs = rodar("native:joinattributesbylocation", INPUT=focos,
                  JOIN=f"{G}|layername=ucs", PREDICATE=[5], JOIN_FIELDS=["nome_uc"],
                  METHOD=0, DISCARD_NONMATCHING=True)

# 5. Count by protected area and satellite
resumo = rodar("qgis:statisticsbycategories", INPUT=focos_ucs,
               CATEGORIES_FIELD_NAME=["nome_uc", "satelite"])
for f in resumo.getFeatures():
    print(f["nome_uc"], f["satelite"], f["count"])
QgsProject.instance().addMapLayer(focos_ucs)
```

The `&field=data_hora_gmt:text` in the layer address forces QGIS to read the date as text, so the filter
works the same in any system language.

## PostGIS

```sql
-- 1. Table for the hotspots and loading of the three files (\copy runs on your computer)
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS artigos.focos;
CREATE TABLE artigos.focos (
    id text, lat numeric, lon numeric, data_hora_gmt timestamp,
    satelite text, municipio text, estado text, pais text,
    municipio_id bigint, estado_id int, pais_id int,
    numero_dias_sem_chuva numeric, precipitacao numeric, risco_fogo numeric,
    bioma text, frp numeric
);
\copy artigos.focos FROM PROGRAM 'curl -s https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/diario/Brasil/focos_diario_br_$(date -u +%Y%m%d).csv' CSV HEADER
\copy artigos.focos FROM PROGRAM 'curl -s https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/diario/Brasil/focos_diario_br_$(date -u -d yesterday +%Y%m%d).csv' CSV HEADER
\copy artigos.focos FROM PROGRAM 'curl -s https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/diario/Brasil/focos_diario_br_$(date -u -d "2 days ago" +%Y%m%d).csv' CSV HEADER

-- 2. Points
ALTER TABLE artigos.focos ADD COLUMN geom geometry(Point, 4674);
UPDATE artigos.focos SET geom = ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(lon, lat), 4674);
CREATE INDEX ON artigos.focos USING gist (geom);

-- 3 to 5. Hotspots in protected areas in the last 24 and 48 hours (time in UTC)
SELECT u.nome_uc,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.data_hora_gmt >= (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - interval '24 hours') AS focos_24h,
       count(*) AS focos_48h,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.satelite = 'AQUA_M-T') AS focos_48h_referencia
FROM artigos.focos f
JOIN artigos.ucs u ON ST_Within(f.geom, u.geom)
WHERE f.data_hora_gmt >= (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - interval '48 hours'
GROUP BY u.nome_uc
ORDER BY focos_48h DESC;
```

::: {.callout-note}
`\copy … FROM PROGRAM` needs `curl`, and on Windows replace `$(date …)` with the date written by hand.
Another option is to download the files first and use `\copy artigos.focos FROM 'focos.csv' CSV HEADER`.
:::

## Python

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd

url = ("https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/diario/"
       "Brasil/focos_diario_br_{}.csv")

# 1. Download today, yesterday and the day before
agora = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
dias = [(agora - timedelta(days=i)).strftime("%Y%m%d") for i in range(3)]
focos = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(url.format(d)) for d in dias], ignore_index=True)
focos["data_hora_gmt"] = pd.to_datetime(focos["data_hora_gmt"], utc=True)

# 2. Points and 3. last 48 hours
focos = gpd.GeoDataFrame(focos, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(focos.lon, focos.lat), crs=4674)
focos = focos[focos["data_hora_gmt"] >= agora - timedelta(hours=48)]
focos["janela"] = (focos["data_hora_gmt"] >= agora - timedelta(hours=24)).map(
    {True: "last 24 h", False: "24 to 48 h"})

# 4. Which protected area (or surroundings) each hotspot fell in
G = "dados/artigos.gpkg"
zonas = pd.concat([
    gpd.read_file(G, layer="ucs")[["nome_uc", "geometry"]].assign(local="interior"),
    gpd.read_file(G, layer="ucs_entorno")[["nome_uc", "geometry"]].assign(local="entorno"),
])
focos_ucs = gpd.sjoin(focos, zonas, predicate="within")

# 5. Count
print(pd.crosstab([focos_ucs["nome_uc"], focos_ucs["local"]], focos_ucs["janela"],
                  margins=True, margins_name="total"))
print(focos_ucs[focos_ucs["satelite"] == "AQUA_M-T"].groupby("nome_uc").size())
focos_ucs.to_file("dados/focos_ucs_48h.gpkg")
```

:::

## Checking the result

The numbers change every run. On the afternoon of 2026-10-29, the three tested versions found the same
hotspots inside the protected areas of the study area:

| Protected area | Last 24 h | Last 48 h | 48 h, `AQUA_M-T` only | Surroundings, 48 h |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Tapajós Environmental Protection Area | 17 | 34 | 5 | 41 |
| Altamira National Forest | 5 | 8 | 4 | 0 |
| Jamanxim National Forest | 0 | 8 | 0 | 3 |
| Iriri State Forest | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Pouso Alto Environmental Protection Area (Cerrado) | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |

: Fire hotspots inside and around protected areas, queried on 2026-10-29 at 4:40 pm (Brasília time). {.striped}

The same 52 hotspots inside the protected areas in all three versions. The difference between the
all-satellites column (34) and the reference-satellite column (5) for the Tapajós Environmental
Protection Area shows why you should not add up satellites to compare periods.

## Running it on its own every day

This is the kind of script worth **scheduling**:

- **Windows:** Task Scheduler, calling `propy.bat script.py` (ArcGIS Pro) or `python script.py`.
- **ArcGIS Pro 3.x:** right-click the script tool → **Schedule**.
- **Linux/Mac:** `crontab -e` and a line such as `0 7 * * * cd /dados && python focos.py`.

To avoid piling up duplicate rows at each run, see
[Updating layers without duplicates](13-updating-layers.qmd).

## Pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning}
## Time in UTC
The `data_hora_gmt` field is in **UTC** (Brasília = UTC−3). If you filter "last 24 hours" using the
computer clock, you lose or gain 3 hours of hotspots. Compute the cutoff in UTC, as in the code above.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Counting hotspots from all satellites
On the same day, the study area had hotspots from 7 satellites. Adding them all gives a larger number
that changes with the satellites in operation. To compare years or months, use only `AQUA_M-T` (the
reference satellite). To alert the brigade, use all of them.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Today's file is incomplete
The current day's file grows during the day. That is why the code downloads **three** files: only then
is the last 48 hours complete at any time of day.
:::
